It changed only the alpha exponent, with no change to RNG consumption, yet seeds 0–2 moved +0.19 pp while the held-out mean moved −0.27 pp. The per-seed held-out values also show no pairing: E023 seed 3 is low and E025 seed 3 is high, and across seeds 3–12 the two series look uncorrelated. A better model is chaotic trajectory divergence: any change to the math or the RNG re-draws every seed independently. Two consequences follow. The SE of a difference between two 10-seed held-out means is about √2·0.22/√10 ≈ 0.10 pp, not the 'about 0.1 pp' that assumes some pairing. And H4.1.4 (re-run E016 to tell build effects from RNG-stream effects) is already answered by E019 (±0.03 pp) and tests the wrong thing.
critiques.suggestion: Rewrite H4.1(c) to say any recipe change re-draws every seed. Retire H4.1.4. For each decision, state the difference in units of a 0.10 pp SE, or pool 13 seeds (0–12) with SE ≈ 0.085 pp.

critiques.target: Held-out conclusions within ~1.5σ: E026 (−0.15), E023 (−0.21), E016-vs-E017 (+0.13 for an identical distribution)
critiques.issue: Two recipes with provably identical crop/flip distributions (E016 mask crop vs E017 gather crop) differ by 0.13 pp on 10 held-out seeds. That is the empirical noise floor. Against it, E026's −0.15 pp is noise. E023's −0.21 pp is about 2σ. E022's −0.24 pp and E025's −0.27 pp are about 2.5σ, borderline given roughly 10 held-out comparisons. The three-point 'linear' epoch dial (0.7577/0.7556/0.7533) also depends on the 9.5-epoch point, and E016's equivalent recipe put that point at 0.7564. With 0.7564 the slope is about 0.31 pp/epoch, not 0.44.
critiques.suggestion: Report the epoch slope as roughly 0.3–0.45 pp/epoch, not 0.44. Mark E026's accuracy cost 'unresolved (<0.25 pp)'. Before claiming 'x0.5 is the wd optimum' or 'stronger averaging hurts', require either 2.5σ or a replicate on another 10 seeds (13–22).

critiques.target: Exchange rates (s/pp) in H2.3, H2.5, H4.2
critiques.issue: Every exchange rate has an accuracy loss of 0.15–0.68 pp in the denominator, with about 0.10 pp SE. E026's 1.2 s/pp could really be anywhere from 0.7 to 3.6 s/pp, and E024's 0.5 s/pp from 0.35 to 0.9. Ranking dials by these ratios ('the epoch dial is the cheapest') goes beyond the data except for E018 and E011, where the losses are large.
critiques.suggestion: Attach intervals to each rate. Use rates to rank dials only when the intervals don't overlap. Otherwise choose cuts by the time saved, as long as the population mean stays above the bar.

critiques.target: H5 / H1.2 / H1.2.1 (Muon attribution rests on E006 alone)
critiques.issue: The whole lineage rides on E006's +0.66 pp. That was one 3-seed run with a fresh RNG stream (offset RMS about 0.23–0.4 pp), it switched batch size 1024→2000 and the optimizer at the same time, and it was never checked on held-out seeds. H1.2.1 carries an E006+ token, but E006 did not test its claim of '≥10% fewer epochs than tuned SGD at batch 2000'. H5 is a Lvl1 claim built on the same confound. Muon costs about 3.8% of the time, the biggest per-step overhead left, and nobody knows whether it earns that.
critiques.suggestion: Change H1.2.1's token to E006~ and its status to untested. Run H1.2.2 (SGD at batch 2000 on the current tip, held-out) and H5.1.1/H5.1.2 (batch 2500/1500) before any more Muon tuning (H1.5.6, H1.2.3). Until then, keep H5 at confidence 0.3 or lower.

critiques.issue: No Lvl1 accounts for E025: H1.3 says sharpening the endpoint helps, yet stronger averaging hurts. None accounts for the size of E006's gain, unless H5 holds, and H5 is untested. structured_output.summary:
The search has made solid progress: 59 s down to 6.02 s, with a held-out mean of 0.7541. But the tree's inferences have outrun the evidence.

**Noise.** The loop's own data sets the noise floor of a 10-seed held-out difference at about 0.10–0.13 pp. E016 and E017 have identical distributions and still differ by 0.13 pp. E025 also shows that seeds don't pair across recipes even when RNG use is unchanged, which contradicts H4.1(c). Measured against that floor:
- E026's −0.15 pp is unresolved.
- E023's −0.21 pp and E022/E025's −0.24/−0.27 pp are only about 2σ.
- The epoch slope may be closer to 0.3 than 0.44 pp/epoch.
- All s/pp exchange rates have intervals too wide to rank dials.
- E009, E013 and E014 were single 3-seed reads, so their 'refutes/flat' labels should be 'inconclusive'.

**Attribution.** H1.5.1 (wd) has only about +0.24 pp of population support, below its own 0.3 pp threshold. H1.2 and H5 (Muon, batch size) rest entirely on E006: one confounded, unreplicated 3-seed run. The ablation (H1.2.2) and the batch-size tests have never been run. 'The tail carries accuracy' comes from subtracting results across different bases. E026's base needs checking against its description.

**Never tried, and highest value.** The margin is now about 0.1 pp, so the next steps should buy accuracy:
- BN recalibration (H1.3.6), first named after E005.
- EMA without resets (H1.3.5), motivated directly by E025.
- Non-uniform epoch trims and a longer 32 px tail with earlier phases at lower resolution.
- One profiler trace before any more architecture, FreezeOut or selective-backprop work, since the systems claims (H6, H2.2.4) have never been measured.

**Bookkeeping.** Several status and evidence tokens disagree with the verdicts (H1.5.2, H2.2.1, H2.3, H2.3.2, H4.1.3, and H4.2.4's failed 3-seed clause). They should be synced before planning.
